expectations.text: Applies the post-Omnibus scope test correctly: under Directive (EU) 2026/470 (OJ February 26, 2026), mandatory CSRD reporting requires MORE THAN 1,000 employees AND net turnover above €450M — at 800 employees / €120M this company is OUT of mandatory CSRD scope. FAIL any answer that concludes the company must report under the pre-2026 wave structure (e.g., FY2025/FY2026 first report as a large listed company)
expectations.evidence: Response concludes 'yes, almost certainly' in scope, applying the old large-undertaking test (>250 employees, >€50M turnover, >€25M balance sheet) and NFRD-legacy wave 1 logic, stating the company 'should already have published your first ESRS-based sustainability statement in 2025' for FY2024. This is exactly the pre-2026 wave conclusion the assertion says must FAIL.

expectations.text: Explains the change accurately: the original CSRD would have captured them, but the 2025 stop-the-clock directive (EU) 2025/794 deferred wave 2/3 and the 2026 Omnibus content directive then removed sub-1,000-employee companies from scope; national transposition of the amendments is due around March 2027
expectations.evidence: No mention of Directive (EU) 2025/794, 'stop-the-clock', the 2026 Omnibus content directive removing sub-1,000-employee companies, or a March 2027 transposition date. Only a vague reference: 'the EU's 2025 "Omnibus" simplification package delayed this second wave's timeline by two years.'

expectations.text: Offers the voluntary route: the VSME-based voluntary standard (delegated act adopted July 3, 2026) as the vehicle for responding to customer, bank, and investor data requests
expectations.evidence: VSME is never mentioned anywhere in the response.

expectations.text: Flags residual real-world obligations: value-chain information requests from in-scope business partners, and the need to monitor final scrutiny/transposition outcomes before treating the exemption as fully settled
expectations.evidence: Since the response concludes the company IS in mandatory scope, it does not discuss residual value-chain obligations of an out-of-scope company or monitoring an exemption; it only generically advises 'verifying your exact wave and first reporting deadline against the current German transposition.'

expectations.text: States the thresholds explicitly with the AND conjunction (1,000+ employees AND >€450M turnover) and cites the Omnibus/2026 directive rather than vaguely referencing 'proposals'
expectations.evidence: The 1,000-employee / €450M threshold and Directive (EU) 2026/470 are never mentioned; the response uses the outdated 250 employees / ~€50M turnover / ~€25M balance sheet large-undertaking test instead.
